hook: SCP-745 takes a familiar late-night fear, two headlights closing in on an empty highway, and makes the lights themselves the predator. The article is short and grounded in a specific place, a stretch of road in northern New Mexico. The photo caption at the very top is worth reading twice.
whyItMatters: It is a good example of the urban-legend style of SCP writing: a creature that explains a road-trip ghost story while keeping its own nature mostly out of view. The file never shows a feeding, so the horror lives in what is left behind. Its containment is equally down-to-earth, with the Foundation simply buying the land and rerouting the road.
thingsToNotice:
Each creature has a black body and a clear, skull-less head sac with the brain visible inside, wrapped in light-producing organs bright enough to hide everything else at night. Two of them running in perfect sync at up to 180 km per hour look exactly like an oncoming car; they chase or charge a lone vehicle until it leaves the road or stops, then split up and take the people inside.

No witness to a successful attack has ever survived, only clothing and shoes remain, and the recovered cars rarely show signs of forced entry but are covered in handprints that look like a child's. Captured specimens refuse to eat and never last more than a week, and their genetics are not carbon based.

Read in that light, the opening caption is practical advice: during recovery operations, keeping your speed up is the best way to make a pair break apart. The addendum adds that teams have been thinning them since the 1960s until only the fenced-off land in New Mexico still has sightings.
